title: Kinematics with calculus
examples: How do I find the total distance travelled if the velocity changes direction?
Is displacement always positive, or can it be negative?
What is the relationship between the integral of velocity and displacement?

explain.say: Today we look at motion using calculus concepts. We relate position, velocity, and acceleration.
Velocity is the rate of change of position. Mathematically, velocity is the derivative of position. We write this as v equals d s divided by d t.
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. Therefore, acceleration is the derivative of velocity. We write this as a equals d v divided by d t.

Displacement is the net change in position. It is found by integrating the velocity function over a time interval. For example, the displacement from time zero to time four is the integral of v dt from zero to four.
Distance travelled is the total path length covered. To find this, we must integrate the speed, which is the absolute value of velocity. So, distance is the integral of the absolute value of v dt.

items: Integrate the absolute value of velocity

faq.q: What is the difference between displacement and distance?
faq.a: Displacement is just the final position minus the starting position. Distance is the total length of the path you actually walked or travelled.

faq.q: If velocity is negative, does that mean the object is moving backward?
faq.a: Yes, in one dimension, a negative velocity means the object is moving in the negative direction. It is moving away from the origin.

faq.q: Why do I use the absolute value when calculating distance?
faq.a: We use the absolute value because distance must always be a positive quantity. We care about how far you went, not the direction you went.
asks: Why not just integrate v dt for distance?
How do I make velocity positive for distance?

faq.q: Does the integral of acceleration give me velocity?
faq.a: Yes, integrating acceleration with respect to time gives you the change in velocity. This is a fundamental relationship in calculus.
asks: What is the integral of a?
How do I get v from a?

faq.q: If the velocity graph crosses the t-axis, what does that mean?
faq.a: When the velocity graph crosses the time axis, it means the object momentarily stops moving. Its velocity is zero at that exact point.

When is the object at rest?

facts: Velocity is the derivative of position with respect to time.
Acceleration is the derivative of velocity with respect to time.
Displacement is calculated by integrating the velocity function.
Distance travelled requires integrating the speed, which is the absolute value of velocity.

quiz.say: The displacement from t=0 to t=2, given v(t) = 3t - 1, is:
quiz.why: You integrate the velocity function and evaluate it at the given limits, which gives the net change in position.

wrong.1: This is the value of v(1), which is only the velocity at one instant, not the total change.
wrong.2: This is the value of v(2), which only tells you the final velocity, not the total displacement.
wrong.3: This is the value of v(0), which is the initial velocity and ignores the movement over time.

quiz.say: If position s(t) = t^2 + 2t, what is the velocity at t=3?
quiz.why: You find the derivative of the position function to get velocity, and then substitute t=3 into that new function.

wrong.0: This incorrectly calculates s(3) + 3, confusing position with velocity.
wrong.2: This is the value of s(3), which is the position, not the rate of change of position.
wrong.3: This is the constant term from the derivative, ignoring the time dependence of the velocity.
